To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the turbulence modeling has a strong influence on the prediction of the flow behavior and that the modified k e and k o SST model are able to predict the unsteadiness of cloud cavitation with a good agreement.

the present work confirms the ability of RANS modeling to reproduce the main characteristics of cloud cavitation; the modification of the turbulence models proposed in [1,2] improves the results, especially for the NACA hydrofoil case, but some discrepancies remain, in particular concerning the turbulent shear stress; the role of the transport term in the k e RNG model is highlighted, and the validity of the assumption of Bradshaw for adverse pressure gradient flows is discussed.
the present study demonstrates the capability of the homogeneous RANS approach with the modified k e and k o turbulence models to reproduce the unsteady behavior of cloud cavitation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new algorithm for the numerical modeling of unsteady caviation, and with the study of its influence on the results.
the development of a new algorithm based on the implicit fractional step method for the solution of the time dependent transport equation for the vapor volume fraction.
the development of a new numerical algorithm for the simulation of unsteadiness of cloud cavitation and its application to a Venturi type section as well as to a NACA 0015 hydrofoil.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a modified k o SST model is the best option for the prediction of cloud cavitation flows, while the k e RNG model should be used with caution.
the modified turbulence models can be successfully applied for the numerical simulation of cloud cavitation flows, but the results are still affected by some uncertainties.
the turbulence modeling is a crucial issue for the simulation of unsteadiness in cavitating flows, and that the use of a modified k o SST model is recommended for the present application.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a proper modeling of the turbulent shear stress is essential to reproduce cloud cavitation, but it is not sufficient.
the modified k e and k o SST model is able to reproduce the main characteristics of unsteady caviation.

the present approach, based on an homogeneous model coupled with a RANS framework, can be successfully applied to simulate unsteady cavitatin flows, and that the modification of the turbulence model is necessary for the prediction of the unsteadiness of the flow.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the modification of the turbulence model alone cannot be considered sufficient to accurately predict cloud cavitation flows.
